..
As of 930 PM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Breezy and mostly sunny Fall-like week for most.
Breezy NNE winds continue through the middle of the week, with 
mainly dry conditions expected. Cool nights prevail well inland with
lighter winds. 

IR and nighttime physics satellite imagery showing that the
strato-cu across the far SE has mostly dissipated this evening,
with a mainly clear sky area-wide. Sprawling low pressure
remains several hundred miles offshore of the NC OBX. Outside 
of the wind along the coast, the weather should be remarkably 
uneventful this week as high pressure keeps most of us sunny and
temperatures around seasonable levels. Dry conditions are also 
expected to prevail with low and comfortable humidity values. 
Should note there is a low (<20%) chance of a rogue shower along
the immediate VA and NC coast Tuesday night into Wednesday 
morning as the low potentially retrogrades westward a bit, but 
this would be dependent on the exact position of the low. 

Regarding temperature specifics, have lowered tonight's (early 
AM Tuesday) min temps a few degrees based on current conditions,
going close to the MAV values along and W of I-95. It will not 
be as favorable as last night when ~1035mb sfc high pressure was
centered over the piedmont, but expect to see lows into the 
upper 30s for most of the northern piedmont, with pockets of mid
30s possible. Added patchy frost wording to Louisa/Fluvanna, 
but do not anticipate this being widespread so did not issue a
Frost Advisory. Elsewhere, lows will mostly range in the low-mid
40s, with 50s near the coast where mixing continues with
elevatedN-NE winds.

Highs Tuesday through Thursday should be a bit warmer than 
today, generally in the upper 60s to lower 70s. A push of cold 
advection cools Friday off a bit, but not excessively so. The 
current temperature forecast ranges from around 60 F on the 
Eastern Shore to the low to mid 60s for mainland VA and NC. The 
dry and seasonable wx should continue into the upcoming weekend,
with the leftovers of the nor'easter/coastal system well 
northeast of the area and across the extreme eastern Canadian 
Maritimes by this time. Overnight lows remain on the chilly side
and should average in the 40s inland and 50s near the coast. It
could dip into the upper 30s in the rural locations well 
inland, with the best chances for this Wednesday night and 
Friday night. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Water levels gradually rise this week. Coastal 
Flood Advisories are in effect today into Wednesday night 
across the lower Chesapeake Bay, lower James River, and the 
Atlantic coast.

Prolonged onshore flow will produce tidal anomalies of 1 to 2 feet 
above normal astronomical tides. Fortunately, the region is 
currently in an astronomical neap tide cycle, which will help 
mitigate peak water levels. Even so, widespread minor to locally 
moderate coastal flooding is expected during high tides through mid 
to late week. All Coastal Flood Watches have been converted to 
Coastal Flood Advisories, with areas along the southern James River, 
southern Chesapeake Bay, Virginia Beach, and eastern Currituck (in 
previous Coastal Flood Advisory) now in effect through Wednesday 
afternoon's high tide and areas on the southern and coastal MD/VA 
Eastern Shore in effect with Tuesday afternoon's high tide through 
Wednesday afternoon's high tide.

Tidal levels are expected to gradually increase through Wednesday, 
with higher levels possible each day. The tidal anomalies currently 
are not trending as high as previous forecasts, which will result in 
nuisance to marginal minor flood stage tonight and early Tuesday's 
high tides along areas in the previous Coastal Flood Advisory. With 
the lower anomalies and lower NNE wind gusts, guidance has trended 
toward more widespread minor tidal flooding, rather than widespread 
moderate to locally major tidal flooding. It is likely that the 
current Advisories will need extended in time to capture Thursday's 
high tides. In addition, Coastal Flood Advisories will likely be 
need for the mid-upper Chesapeake Bay by Wednesday into the later 
portion of the week. There is also at least a signal that Bishop's 
Head may approach moderate flood stage Wednesday night or Thursday. 
A localized Coastal Flood Warning may be needed later in this week 
for any localized moderate stage flooding, depending on trends.
